prompt: A flat layered paper-cut collage in a strict handcraft design system: everything is cut from colored cardstock and hanji paper with perfectly clean cut edges — NO outline of any kind on any piece: no bright edge line, no white edge, no dark contour line. Each object is built from two to five completely flat die-cut pieces layered ON THE OBJECT ITSELF — its own silhouette, a main color piece, one or two detail pieces and a highlight piece — the object is never placed on a base, platform, pedestal, plinth or pile of paper sheets; Every upper piece sits slightly RAISED above the piece beneath it, so along EVERY boundary where two different colors meet, the upper piece casts a soft narrow warm dark-brown shadow down onto the lower piece — a gentle embossed paper relief wherever two colors touch, and this relief shadow is the ONLY depth cue. Cut economy: every scissor cut is purposeful and confident — a shape that is straight in the real object is cut with a clean STRAIGHT edge, and curves appear ONLY where the real object is actually curved. No decorative wavy edges, no bumpy wobbly outlines, no gratuitous scalloping on untextured surfaces; a rectangular block is cut as a plain rectangle, though corners may be gently ROUNDED — softly rounding a corner is natural scissor work. Shapes stay simple and chunky, no detail finer than real scissors could cut. Scalloped repeat patterns for textures like straw or waves, cut big and loose. Strictly straight-on orthographic front view, zero perspective. No volume, no curvature, no folded paper, no sculpting. Real-scissors discipline: every piece is a shape that could actually be cut with scissors from a single sheet of colored paper. EACH PIECE IS EXACTLY ONE SOLID FLAT COLOR — no gradient, no shading, no airbrush, no painted detail inside a piece; every color change is a separate stacked paper piece, even a thin line is its own paper strip. ALL pieces share one identical fine colored-paper texture. All shadows are neutral warm dark-brown paper shadows, never colored. A premium layered paper-cut illustration, wide landscape 16:9 format, composed as FULL-BLEED key art that fills the whole frame edge to edge. There is NO white page and NO margin: the artwork itself is the entire picture. FOUR or FIVE THICK torn-paper rings in the shape of a round pumpkin carriage silhouette step inward from the frame edges — the outer rings are so large that they extend beyond and are cropped by the edges of the frame, colours stepping from pale sky blue at the outermost to periwinkle to deep navy toward the centre, each ring a clearly visible WIDE band casting a soft shadow on the next, strong obvious depth like layered paper waves. The deepest centre layer, filling at least 70 percent of the whole picture, is a detailed layered paper-cut diorama of the key scene: a palace ballroom at night with a grand staircase, a big clock showing almost midnight, a golden pumpkin coach waiting, two little white mice, and a sparkling glass slipper resting on a stair step in front. Composition is landscape: the ballroom spreads wide across the frame with the staircase on the right, the clock top-center, the coach at the left. The BOTTOM QUARTER of the frame is a calm soft low-contrast band of deep navy paper with only gentle texture and no detail, where a title can be placed. Elegant, harmonious, soft light from the top left. Cute Korean picture-book style for 3-4 year olds, never scary. No text.
